name: A New Century · overlapping social groups
description: Govern for five years: keep household needs met, services funded and government stable. Country play continues after political transitions. Relative food/energy prices are authored rules-3 model assumptions, not sourced historical prices. The original fixed-price pack is retained for classic saves. Borrowing authority, consent delays and emergency political costs are authored rules-4 assumptions, not a reproduction of historical debt law. Earlier market and classic packs remain available for their original campaigns. Constitutional transitions use authored rules-5 templates, backing thresholds, costs and inertia rather than sourced historical amendment law. Starter AI prefers its opening governing form; fictional fixtures demonstrate alternative preferences. Earlier campaigns retain their original packs. Policy amendments, withdrawal, history and observed reviews use authored rules-6 procedures. Existing campaigns retain their exact original rules. Ministerial portfolios, generated nominees and preparation rules are authored gameplay definitions, not historical ministry rosters or vacancy claims. Unassigned portfolios use permanent civil service. Earlier campaigns retain their exact original rules. Independent electoral mandates, early-poll powers and calendar terms are authored gameplay assumptions, not historical national election law. Earlier campaigns retain their exact original rules. Population observations cover all 15 starter countries and GDP covers 14, from the pinned World Bank mirrors. North Korean GDP retains its explicit authored calibration. Annual observations are bookmark proxies; primary sources have not been independently reconciled. National/local budget charters and territorial procedures are authored gameplay abstractions. The two disjoint budget jurisdictions per country are population partitions, not historical administrative units, mapped boundaries or regional electorates. Local purchase levels, collected-tax shares, autonomy templates, compensation and consent proxies are original model assumptions. Public delivery pledges, governing support arrangements and linked project deadlines use authored procedures and credibility records, not historical campaign promises or party agreements. They do not supply resources or form cabinet coalitions. Existing policy authority and implementation constraints apply. Reviewed annual and supplementary fiscal packages use authored preparation, administration, implementation reservation and calendar accounting procedures. Enactment funds actual policy programmes; recurring purchasing remains subject to cash and delivery constraints. These plans are not historical budget laws or hard appropriation ceilings. Progressive private-income withholding uses authored representative-cohort bands relative to opening GDP per resident, not historical filing law or within-cohort distributions. Public/local service payments and welfare remain outside this base. Potential tax is not treasury cash or arrears. Nonplayer fiscal reviews use the national daily balance after protected local tax claims. A consolidated surplus cannot finance national obligations from protected local cash. Budget authority, submission funding, review and actual programme delivery remain ordinary shared constraints. This is an authored bounded heuristic, not historical government behavior or optimal economic planning. New loan principal matures an authored 365 days after actual disbursement. Opening debt remains perpetual calibration; historical debt curves and actual refinancing markets are not claimed. Temporary cash retention can protect actual national funds for a future decision, up to 1% opening GDP for 90 days, with approval cost and reuse cooldown. Unfunded targets are not cash. Release, expiry or a successor government ends protection without cancelling obligations or granting spending authority. Debt interest accrues at fixed 4% actual/365 on actual outstanding principal after scheduled redemption. Fractions carry without compounding until a whole reporting unit becomes due; only paid amounts transfer cash. Unpaid whole interest remains external arrears, while the unsettled sub-unit creditor claim survives principal retirement without becoming cash or spending authority. Tax, wage, purchase and price rounding remain whole reporting units. Existing grid and agriculture programmes have explicitly authored technology eligibility for every seeded country from the 2000 bookmark. Eligibility grants no research, adoption, cash, capacity or faster construction; ordinary authority, funding and delivery remain necessary. These dates are scenario permissions, not historical discovery or adoption records. Independently authored party fiscal ranges add delayed political tradeoffs for operating income-tax, service and welfare policies. Legislative coalitions use live seat weights; party leadership uses its ruling party. Unknown positions remain explicit, and other governing routes retain independent backing. No positions are inferred from ideology labels or claimed as sourced historical platforms. Preferences grant no resources, consent exemptions or free support. Social, institutional, regional and foreign-policy positions and dated platform evolution remain unfinished. Reference sovereignty geography remains unknown. National food and energy reserves start empty. Ordinary consent and paid administration authorize finite import contracts at fixed quoted prices, with full purchase cash reserved. Deliveries require spare import capacity after civilian physical needs; proposal and consent create no goods. Stored goods automatically cover post-import physical shortfalls. Food spoilage and household affordability remain binding; cancellation or expiry releases only unspent purchase reservations. These are generic model equivalents, not historical national stockpiles or storage technologies. Events carry stable country-scoped software references across filtering, retained history and save/load. References reveal only retained owner events, are never reused after expiry and grant no resources or legal powers. Failed reference allocation rolls back the command or incomplete daily step. Earlier packs retain their exact definitions and behavior. Policy lifecycle events identify their owned programme and recorded stage directly. Chronicle inspection opens the real pending or historical record; outcome reviews remain observations rather than isolated causal estimates. Earlier content packs retain their original event encoding and replay behavior. The authored 100-seat election rule allocates remaining seats across opposition parties in ascending stable party-ID order. The largest opposition party leads a successor coalition; equal seat totals choose the lowest stable party ID. Display names and input row order do not settle these choices. Older rules retain their original ordering. This is a reproducible game abstraction, not a claim about national electoral laws. Optional stable person/office/currency references cover only the existing opening labels on 2000-01-01 (exclusive end 2000-01-02). The IDs, roles and one-day coverage are authored metadata, not verified historical term dates. Separate executive and party leaders remain separate; an explicitly collective party leadership has no invented named members. Missing other offices remain unknown. Later bookmark coverage is absent; these references never schedule campaign handovers or add authority, resources or policy effects. The default starter and every previous pack remain unchanged. Older review observations are retained as calendar-year sample summaries after leaving the 120-review recent window. This changes statistical retention only; it grants no resources or authority. All earlier rules packs keep their original behavior. Authored statutory prototype: higher new service programmes require a paid, consented and implemented legal authority. This is an original scenario rule, not a historical statement of national legislation. Stable live holder references and separately identified simulated successor bodies. Opening people and offices remain source references; future source terms do not force campaign outcomes. Authored stable identities for modeled governing routes and submission context. These are gameplay institutions, without claims about historical names, membership, founding dates or votes. Optional authored demographic exercise: every country uses the same coarse birth, mortality, age-split, family-formation and statistical-capacity assumptions. These are not historical national vital statistics, census quality rankings or migration estimates. Aggregate household units create no dwellings or wealth. Working age is not employment. Production and import capacity remain tied to opening physical need; new residents increase civilian demand without creating capacity. GDP remains an opening calibration. Migration moves residents between country/cohort stocks, without transferring pooled group cash, assets or arrears. Pooled claims and already-funded local financial obligations remain payable even if a cohort becomes empty; those transfers do not certify staffing or actual service delivery. Regional placement, housing constraints, individual labor mobility, inheritance and endogenous fertility remain unfinished. Authored cross-sectional joint membership profiles, not historical national prevalence, individual identity histories or records about real residents. Disjoint age/employment scopes prevent double-counting people. The employment membership reproduces existing modeled jobs; membership grants no cash, votes, powers or programme exemptions. Joint shares are explicitly configured, without assuming independent memberships. Parent/carer membership uses the model's 15+ bands, not a claim about legal adulthood. Union membership in this exercise is limited to modeled employed residents; retiree/other union membership and longitudinal joining/leaving remain unfinished. These common assumptions are shared across countries and economic cohorts.

No historical election promises, party agreements, commercial contracts or treaties are claimed.

Original annual/supplementary fiscal preparation, institutional review, administration costs, implementation reservations and calendar execution. No historical budget law, tax-base calibration or hard appropriation ceiling is claimed.

Original representative-cohort private-income bands, GDP-per-resident thresholds, marginal rate factors and fixed 365-day annualisation. No historical tax filing law, individual distributions or national tax-base calibration is claimed.

Original national-funding review objective for the bounded fiscal AI. It respects protected local claims and shared legal/cash/implementation rules; it does not claim historical government decisions, privileged revenue or optimal planning.

Original 365-day maturity and scheduled-principal settlement for new loans. Existing authority and emergency constraints are retained; this is not historical debt calibration or default/restructuring.

Original temporary retention of actual national cash after protected local and capital claims. Deferred operating payments remain arrears; unpaid principal remains debt. Uniform authored gameplay procedure, not historical cash-management law or payment priority.

Original fixed 4% actual/365 principal-day accrual with carried fractional reporting units. Whole interest due, actual cash payments and unpaid whole-unit arrears reconcile separately. This is uniform gameplay accounting, not historical debt pricing, compounding, currency precision or legal settlement law.

Original baseline programme eligibility for the 2000 bookmark. All seeded countries may commission the existing grid and agriculture programmes from the bookmark, subject to ordinary funding and governing authority. Dates denote scenario permissions, not historical scientific discovery, knowledge adoption or research completion.

Original party-specific fiscal ranges, relative importance and bounded monthly backing pressure for gameplay. These are not sourced historical platforms or positions inferred from ideology labels. Unknown positions remain explicit; royal, religious, personalist and military routes retain independent backing. Other preference dimensions and dated platform changes remain unknown.

Original costed fixed-price commodity import contracts, spare civilian import capacity, national buffers and automatic shortage releases. National stocks start empty; normalized capacities and contracts are gameplay conventions, not observed warehouses, historical reserves, fuel deposits or electricity-storage technologies.

Original software identity convention for country-scoped event references, retained private chronicle lookup and transactional sequence exhaustion. It asserts no historical observations, resources or political privileges.
Original typed links between private policy lifecycle events and their owned programme records. Inspection grants no resources, policy authority or privileged foreign information.

Original deterministic party-ID ordering for the simplified 100-seat election model, covering remainder seats, equal-seat successor leadership and coalition membership order. This does not represent historical electoral law.

Authored stable person/office crosswalk and one-day opening coverage derived solely from existing starter labels. No independently verified tenure, office creation, party membership, collective membership or currency chronology is asserted. Labels retain the identity-notes source limitations.

Original bounded retention rule: retain 120 recent review observations and summarize older samples by calendar year. Means are floor-rounded review-sample means, not annual accounts or time-weighted daily statistics. Coverage remains explicit; private treasury values are never foreign public data.

policies.name: Standard private-income marginal rate
policies.description: Set the standard marginal reference rate for authored private-income bands. Withholding uses actual private income, representative cohort means and collection capacity; benefits and public/local wages remain outside this base. Full tax filing law and other bases are not modeled.

policies.name: Public service budget
policies.description: Annual spending as % of modeled GDP. Delivery improves gradually and is limited by administrative capacity.

policies.name: Household safety net
policies.description: Annual transfers as % of modeled GDP. Payments reach household accounts only when funded.

policies.name: Energy capacity program
policies.description: Build 15 percentage points of domestic energy coverage. Capital is reserved during consent and paid before implementation; operating costs begin on completion.

policies.name: Food resilience program
policies.description: Build 15 percentage points of food supply. Requires time and funded maintenance.

policies.name: Civil service modernization
policies.description: Increase administrative capacity by 8 points, improving tax collection and service delivery.

policies.name: Negotiate governing support
policies.description: Negotiate with parliamentary partners; adds up to 12 support points for the present government. Bargaining uses administrative resources.

demographics.description: Optional authored demographic exercise: every country uses the same coarse birth, mortality, age-split, family-formation and statistical-capacity assumptions. These are not historical national vital statistics, census quality rankings or migration estimates. Aggregate household units create no dwellings or wealth. Working age is not employment. Production and import capacity remain tied to opening physical need; new residents increase civilian demand without creating capacity. GDP remains an opening calibration. Migration moves residents between country/cohort stocks, without transferring pooled group cash, assets or arrears. Pooled claims and already-funded local financial obligations remain payable even if a cohort becomes empty; those transfers do not certify staffing or actual service delivery. Regional placement, housing constraints, individual labor mobility, inheritance and endogenous fertility remain unfinished.

social_memberships.description: Authored cross-sectional joint membership profiles, not historical national prevalence, individual identity histories or records about real residents. Disjoint age/employment scopes prevent double-counting people. The employment membership reproduces existing modeled jobs; membership grants no cash, votes, powers or programme exemptions. Joint shares are explicitly configured, without assuming independent memberships. Parent/carer membership uses the model's 15+ bands, not a claim about legal adulthood. Union membership in this exercise is limited to modeled employed residents; retiree/other union membership and longitudinal joining/leaving remain unfinished. These common assumptions are shared across countries and economic cohorts.

employment.name: Employed residents
employment.description: All residents holding a modeled job, exactly matching existing paid employment. This grants no additional income or votes.

union.name: Union members
union.description: An authored overlay among modeled employed residents. It grants no organisation powers, legal recognition, votes or programme exemptions.

faith.description: An authored nonexclusive overlay across age bands, without claims about one unified religious organisation or historical national prevalence.
